Modified assessment: “Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace,” but the Committee remains cautious, holding rates at 5.25–5.50% until it gains confidence inflation is sustainably headed to 2%. In the Clarida–Galí–Gertler framework on rule-like monetary policy, this reflects an appropriate, data-dependent reaction to easing but still-elevated inflation. Consistent with Svensson and Woodford’s forecast-targeting approach and the New Keynesian Phillips curve emphasis on expectations, the Fed’s patience helps anchor inflation expectations. Recent “inflation-at-risk” work highlights persistent right-tail inflation risks, which supports continued balance-sheet runoff and guarded guidance. Net tone: mildly positive on growth, restrained on policy.
